title: setWindowDuration does not call _syncBudget, so pending dispatcher mint-debt is excluded from the new rate

classification.assetImpact: No direct asset loss. Announced rate and effective rate diverge until next sync; off-chain monitoring/UI mismatch; MEV surface if a large pending mint-debt coincides with a window-shortening.
attackPath: 1. Dispatcher has large pending mint-debt; in-contract rewardBudget is near zero.
2. Owner calls setWindowDuration(shortDuration). _updatePool runs; rewardRate ~= 0 from tiny budget.
3. Next user calls claim()/stake()/unstake(); _syncBudget pulls the mint-debt and recomputes rate against the shortened window, producing a rate spike.
4. JIT staker who times entry just before step 3 captures the spike.
classification.likelihood: low - requires owner to shorten the window while mint-debt is pending, and a well-timed JIT staker. Self-corrects after first sync.
classification.assumptions: Owner-initiated action (setWindowDuration) with specific state (large unpulled mint-debt).

justification: Low/QA. Operator ordering bug inside an owner-only setter. No permissionless attack path. Self-corrects on the next sync call. MEV spike scenario requires a specific owner action plus timing; not a primary protocol-function impairment. Better placed in the QA bundle as a coding defect with a one-line fix (call _syncBudget before recomputing rate).
